newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unemployment rises to new high in June.
newsitem.headline: French unemployment rises to new high in June.

text.p: French unemployment hit a new record in June, underscoring the challenges facing a new Socialist-led government which campaigned on promises to protect jobs.
Economists said the rise of 17,400 jobless to a record 12.6 percent reported on Thursday was disappointing, especially when taken together with poor consumer spending announced earlier this week.
France's Labour Ministry said June's rise took the total number of people out of work to 3,130,900.
The unemployment rate, calculated on the basis of International Labour Organisation (ILO) norms, rose from 12.5 percent in May.
Although the headline unemployment rate peaked at 12.8 percent in April, a different calculation method was used. Based on the new norms, June's 12.6 percent is a record, the ministry said.

"This is considerably worse than expected and should be seen hand-in-hand with the worse than anticipated spending report," said economist William Thornhill at London-based analyst firm Technical Data.
"The underlying message is that the economic recovery is not as strong as many had anticipated," he said.
Most analysts had forecast a June unemployment rate of 12.5 percent. Markets barely reacted to the higher figure, focusing instead on the strength of the dollar.
Figures released on Tuesday showed French consumer spending fell 2.9 percent in June.
That was seen as unhelpful for an administration relying partly on faster growth to get its finances in order for European monetary union while leaving some elbow room to tackle unemployment.

Economist Patrick Mange at Deutsche Bank in Paris said the jobless figures were "very disappointing" as recent evidence had shown laws aimed at rewarding shorter working hours had produced a net increase in jobs.
But he also said things might stabilise or improve in July, when the economy may have gained speed through a pickup in foreign orders sparked by the strong dollar.

"I certainly do not expect a worsening in July," he said, adding that some employers may have deferred hirings from June when Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's leftist government had only just been elected.
The Labour Ministry said the number of people out of work in June rose by 0.6 percent compared with May. For people under 25 years old, the gain was 0.3 percent.
The rise in unemployment was 0.9 percent for men and 0.2 percent for women.
